citation: 'Residence of Mr. N. B. Ream, 1901 Prairie Avenue.' Halftone plate, photographer uncredited, sharing a page with 'Residence of Dr. H. S. Brown, 4917 Drexel Boulevard'. Rand, McNally & Co.'s Pictorial Chicago (Chicago: Rand, McNally & Co., 1893). Reprinted from the same negative in the 1896 edition.
author: Rand, McNally & Co. (publisher); photographer uncredited
repository: Internet Archive, randmcnallycospi00rand_0 (the 1893 edition), page n96; the 1896 edition is randmcnallycospi1892chic, page n98. Prairie library images a19-pictorial-1893-ream and a19-pictorial-1896-ream; the image store's display copies (kevinrhaas/chicago-images, prairie-1904/files/).
locator: The right-hand plate of the page, printed sideways and about 1.45 degrees off square: the Ream house from across Prairie Avenue to the south-west, the whole street front, the canted south-west corner, the porch and its balcony, the stoop between its cheeks, the cornice, the mansard and its dormers, the south flank's front half and its canted bay; the area fence; a street tree across the front's south part.
rights_note: Published in the United States in 1893 (and again in 1896), so in the public domain. The reference copy committed for the image gate (data/sources/assets/ream_1901_photos_t1903/pictorial_1893_ream_plate.jpg) is the store's display copy of the 1893 page turned upright, levelled by the 1.45 degrees it was printed askew and cropped to the plate; nothing is derived from it as an asset.
access_notes: Read 2026-10-29 (T-3186) from the image store's display copy of the 1893 page, 1600 x 1233 px (sha256 7abdb63399c1f20145f3271dfc6ca855267a27d0fa38ec37cd2b59b2de27e4a8; the Archive's file is 1770 x 1364 px), and of the 1896 page, 1400 x 1118 px (sha256 d841e4a9e5282291b1ba905114722e73eeceb2ff33de7361fda6f7f8ba54fc7b). THE SAME NEGATIVE AS THE '1898' PRINT: the plate's edges fit the chicagology copy (chicagology_1901_ream_1898) by a scale of 1.0049 and a shift of (10.3, 15.7) px with no rotation once the plate is levelled, every one of that copy's eight camera-fit points within 0.5 px and their edge correlation 0.94-0.99 (the street tree's bark and knots, the fence's panels and the branches against the sky coincide), so the chicagology picture is this plate cropped, and the photograph was taken by 1893, not in 1898 as its caption says. The 1896 edition prints the same picture again, turned the other way on its page and reproduced coarser: it supplies nothing the 1893 plate does not.
note: The earliest dated print of the Ream house, and the sharpest copy of the photograph the 1898 front view was solved from: it shows a little more under the fence (the curb and the walk) and resolves the stoop's cheeks better, each pierced under its moulded top by a row of rounded openings. Its camera is the 1898 view's, carried through the image fit (data/reference_views/ream_house_1901_prairie/pictorial_1893_plate.json).
what_it_supplies: a date for the photograph the chicagology copy reproduces: by 1893
the street front's composition, as the 1898 copy does, at slightly better resolution
the stoop's two cheeks pierced by a row of openings under their tops
what_it_does_not_supply: colour: the plate is a monochrome halftone
the north flank, the rear and the brick rear range
any independent view: the 1896 reprint is the same negative
